Authorities ..... ... on 12 April, 2023

Bench: B.R. Sarangi, M.S.Raman
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.

Heard Mr. B. Baug, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr. U.C. Mohanty, learned counsel for opposite party no.4.
3.

The petitioners have filed this writ petition seeking direction to opposite party no.4 to implement the order dated 30.03.2017 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No. 6914 of 2012 and the order dated 10.05.2017 passed in RVWPET No. 91 of 2012, and to pay compensation amount to the petitioners along with 9% interest per annum thereon from 01.09.2010.

4. Mr. B. Baug, learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the land of the petitioners has been acquired for widening of National Highway and for that purpose the petitioners are entitled to compensation.

Due to non-payment of such dues, the petitioners had approached this Court by filing W.P.(C) No. 6914 of 2012, which was disposed of vide order dated 30.03.2017 with the following orders:-
"xxx xxx xxx

Considering the submissions made, the Authorized Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Officer (opposite party no.4) is directed to take steps for release of the awarded compensation amount along with the accrued interest thereon in favour of the petitioners on proper identification within four weeks hence."

It is contended that thereafter review petition bearing RVWPET No. 91 of 2017 was filed seeking review of the order dated 30.03.2017 and this Court, vide order dated 10.05.2017 passed following International Society Of Krishna vs National Highway Authorities ..... ... on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81340975/
1 orders:-
"xxx xxx xxx

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the submission made and keeping in view the fact that the compensation amount has not been deposited with the Bank or with any other financial institution, the review-petitioner is directed to release the compensation amount to the petitioners along with interest payable as provided in law."

5. It is further contended by Mr. B. Baug, learned counsel for the petitioners that till date the order dated 30.03.2017 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No. 6914 of 2012 and the order dated 10.05.2017 passed in RVWPET No. 91 of 2012 have not been complied with by paying compensation and interest thereon to the petitioners.
Therefore, the petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition.

6. Mr. U.C. Mohanty, learned counsel for opposite party no.4 contended that so far as compensation amount is concerned, although the same has already been determined as Rs.43,14,280/- and notice has already been issued to the petitioners to receive the amount, but the petitioners have not received the same till date on the plea of non- grant of any interest.
Therefore, the compensation amount is still lying with the opposite party no.4.

It is further contended that in a similar circumstance, this Court in the case of Ghasinath Sahoo v. National Highway Authority of India &
Ors (W.P.(C) No. 4632 of 2018 disposed of on 15.12.2022) came to hold that so far as payment of interest is concerned, since it is a disputed question of fact, the competent authority can resolve the same by invoking the provisions contained in Sections 3-G to 3-H of the National Highways Act,
1956.

entities.text:
Ghasinath Sahoo v. National Highway Authority of India &
Ors (W.P.(C) No. 4632 of 2018
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By holding so, this Court did not feel inclined to entertain the said writ petition.
Thus, it is contended that instead of approaching the authority concerned, the petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition, which cannot be sustained in the eye of law.

7. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and after going through the records, this Court finds that so far as compensation amount is concerned, since the amount has already been determined and the authority has already issued notice to the petitioners to receive such amount, there is no valid and justifiable reason available for the petitioners not to receive the amount bereft of the claim for grant of interest amount which has been withheld by opposite party no.4.

In the above view of the matter, this Court directs the petitioners to receive the compensation amount barring their claim for grant of interest on the compensation amount which has remained with the authority for such a long period.

So far as interest part is concerned, this Court has already modified the order dated 30.03.2017 passed in RVWPET No. 91 of 2017, vide order dated 10.05.2017, stating inter alia that the interest is payable as provided in law.

Therefore, if the petitioners claim for interest, they have to approach the appropriate forum in accordance with the provisions contained under Sections 3- G to 3-H of the National Highways Act, 1956.
If such approach is made, the authority shall consider the same and pass appropriate order with regard to grant of interest.

Needless to say, if the petitioners appear before the opposite party no.4 on 18.04.2023, on that date opposite party no.4 shall make payment of the compensation amount to them, without prejudice to their claim of interest, which is to be decided in accordance with law.
8. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the writ petition stands disposed of.
